subject: psychiatry
title: Alzheimer Disease, Vascular Dementia, and Frontotemporal Syndromes

steps.tx: **Alzheimer disease** is the most common cause of neurodegenerative dementia, responsible for 60 to 70 percent of cases worldwide. It features an insidious onset and gradual progressive cognitive decline, characteristically beginning with prominent episodic memory impairment, difficulty learning new information, and temporal disorientation.
steps.say: Alzheimer disease is the leading cause of dementia, causing insidious, progressive episodic memory loss and difficulty encoding new information.

vis.alt: Alzheimer disease histopathology comparing extracellular amyloid plaques and intracellular neurofibrillary tangles
vis.caption: Alzheimer disease histopathology comparing extracellular amyloid plaques and intracellular neurofibrillary tangles.

steps.tx: **Amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles** constitute the definitive dual neuropathological hallmarks of Alzheimer disease. Extracellular senile plaques are composed of insoluble beta-amyloid-42 peptides derived from abnormal amyloid precursor protein cleavage, while intracellular tangles consist of hyperphosphorylated tau microtubule-associated protein within degenerating cortical neurons.
steps.say: Pathological hallmarks include extracellular beta-amyloid plaques and intracellular hyperphosphorylated tau neurofibrillary tangles.

left.title: Extracellular Amyloid Plaques
points: Deposited early in cerebral cortex and hippocampus

right.title: Intracellular Neurofibrillary Tangles
points: Correlates directly with cognitive decline severity

steps.tx: **Genetic risk architecture in Alzheimer disease** distinguishes rare early-onset familial forms from common late-onset sporadic disease. Early-onset autosomal dominant Alzheimer disease (onset under 65 years) is caused by mutations in APP on chromosome 21, PSEN1 on chromosome 14, or PSEN2 on chromosome 1.
steps.say: Early-onset familial Alzheimer disease involves APP, PSEN1, and PSEN2 mutations. Late-onset sporadic disease is strongly linked to the APOE epsilon-4 allele.

vis.title: Alzheimer Genetic Architecture
rows: Excessive A-beta-42 production; Down syndrome link
Most common cause of familial AD (onset ~45y)
Impairs A-beta clearance; 12-fold risk if homozygous

steps.tx: **Vascular dementia** is the second most common form of dementia, caused by cerebral ischemic or hemorrhagic injury resulting from large-vessel strokes, small-vessel microvascular disease, or lacunar infarcts. The clinical presentation is classically characterized by abrupt onset, stepwise cognitive deterioration, executive dysfunction, and focal neurological deficits.
steps.say: Vascular dementia causes abrupt, stepwise cognitive decline with focal neurological deficits resulting from multi-infarct cerebrovascular disease.

left.title: Vascular Dementia
points: Brain MRI shows extensive white matter ischemia

right.title: Alzheimer Disease
points: Insidious onset with smooth progressive decline
Absence of early focal neurological motor deficits
Brain MRI shows medial temporal & hippocampal atrophy

steps.tx: **Lewy body dementia** is clinically characterized by a core diagnostic triad: fluctuating cognition with pronounced variations in attention, recurrent detailed visual hallucinations of animals or people, and spontaneous parkinsonian motor features. Neuropathology demonstrates cortical Lewy bodies containing aggregated alpha-synuclein protein.
steps.say: Lewy body dementia presents with fluctuating cognition, vivid visual hallucinations, spontaneous parkinsonism, and extreme neuroleptic sensitivity.

vis.title: Lewy Body Dementia Diagnostic Triad
rows: Marked variations in alertness and attention
Detailed, colorful visions of people or animals
Presents early; usually non-threatening to patient
Precedes or emerges within one year of dementia
Precedes cognitive decline by years or decades

steps.tx: Set the two scans in this picture side by side and compare where brain tissue has been lost. **Pick disease** carves out the frontal and anterior temporal lobes with sharp, knife-edge wasting, while Alzheimer disease spreads atrophy more diffusely through temporoparietal regions. That distribution matches the clinical story: early personality and behaviour change in one, early memory failure in the other patient group.
steps.say: Pick disease wastes frontal and anterior temporal lobes sharply, while Alzheimer disease thins temporoparietal cortex more diffusely. The scan pattern mirrors behaviour versus memory onset.

vis.alt: Coronal brain MRI comparison showing knife-edge frontotemporal atrophy in Pick disease against diffuse temporoparietal atrophy in Alzheimer disease
vis.caption: Coronal brain MRI showing knife-edge frontotemporal atrophy in Pick disease contrasting with diffuse temporoparietal atrophy in Alzheimer disease. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Severe neuroleptic sensitivity in Lewy body dementia** represents a life-threatening pharmacological hazard, wherein administering first-generation antipsychotics like haloperidol precipitates catastrophic irreversible parkinsonian rigidity, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, coma, and sudden death. If psychotic agitation demands medical intervention, low-dose quetiapine is the safest option.
steps.say: First-generation antipsychotics trigger fatal rigidity in Lewy body dementia. Low-dose quetiapine is the safest agent for severe psychotic agitation.

left.title: Neuroleptic Hypersensitivity
points: Up to three-fold elevation in acute mortality

right.title: Safe Pharmacological Choices
points: Strict avoidance of haloperidol and risperidone

steps.tx: **Frontotemporal dementia**, also designated Pick disease, presents in presenile adults aged 45 to 65 with profound early personality alterations, behavioral disinhibition, apathy, loss of empathy, and compulsive hyperorality. In striking contrast to Alzheimer disease, patients completely preserve visuospatial orientation and episodic memory in early stages.
steps.say: Frontotemporal dementia presents early with social disinhibition, personality change, and loss of empathy, while memory remains preserved.

vis.title: Frontotemporal Dementia Subtypes
rows: Disinhibition, apathy, loss of empathy, hyperorality
Loss of word meaning and object naming

steps.tx: **Knife-edge lobar atrophy on neuroimaging** serves as the classic anatomical hallmark of Pick disease, displaying circumscribed, severe gyral shrinkage of the frontal and temporal lobes resembling the blade of a knife. Histopathology demonstrates swollen ballooned neurons (Pick cells) and round, argentophilic intraneuronal inclusion bodies (Pick bodies) containing tau.
steps.say: Pick disease exhibits severe knife-edge lobar atrophy of the frontal and temporal lobes, with silver-staining Pick bodies on histology.

left.title: Pick Disease Pathology
points: Spares posterior parietal and occipital lobes
Round tau-positive Pick bodies on silver stain
